title: Quality of the supervision, training and of the two-way transfer of knowledge between the researcher and the host
content:
## 1.3 Quality of the Supervision, Training and of the Two-way Transfer of Knowledge between the Researcher and the Host

### Spine-dependency notice and scope of confirmed content

This sub-section addresses the identity spine of the fellowship — the supervisor, host organisation, and fellowship type determining the applicable knowledge-transfer model. All four spine-identity items bearing on this sub-section — SUPERVISOR, HOST, FELLOWSHIP_TYPE, and DURATION — carry status Unresolved in the confirmation checklist (confirmation_checklist.json; still_requires_real_confirmation: true for all four). No source vault node names any supervisor; the confirmation checklist records source_vault_nodes: [] for the SUPERVISOR token and explicitly characterises this as 'notable for an MSCA-PF, which is supervisor-centric' (confirmation_checklist.json). The synthetic working spine (SYN-SPINE-01), declared under a §3 operator override of §13.3 and logged in decision_log/synthetic-spine-demo-override_2026-07-13.json, supplies placeholder values: [SUPERVISOR — Unresolved; synthetic working value: Prof. Dr. Gábor Nagy [SYNTHETIC], ELTE, environmental physics/geoinformatics] and [HOST — Unresolved; synthetic working value: Eötvös Loránd University (ELTE), Budapest, Hungary [SYNTHETIC ARRANGEMENT]]. These are not real facts; nothing built on them is submittable.

What is confirmed from programme-level Tier 2B sources is the structural training architecture. SR-06 (scope_requirements.json, Confirmed, mandatory) prescribes the mandatory training dimensions. SR-07 (scope_requirements.json, Confirmed, mandatory) prescribes the Career Development Plan structure, joint-authorship requirement, delivery timing, and content dimensions. WP4 (wp_structure.json, Phase 3 output, Confirmed) is the confirmed structural work package housing all training and transfer activities. The expected outcomes EO-01, EO-04, EO-05, EO-07, and EO-08 (expected_outcomes.json, all Confirmed as programme-level call expected outcomes) govern the evaluator criteria this sub-section addresses. Their mappings to the concept: EO-07 Confirmed, EO-01 Confirmed, EO-04 Assumed, EO-05 Inferred, EO-08 Inferred (concept_refinement_summary.json). The supervisor's track record, host's specific supervision infrastructure, and numerical training targets beyond what SR-06/SR-07 mandates remain Unresolved or spine-dependent and are flagged as such throughout.

---

### The dedicated training and supervision work package: WP4

WP4 — Training, Supervision and Two-way Transfer of Knowledge — is the structural work package within which all CDP governance, training programme delivery, and knowledge-transfer activities are housed (wp_structure.json, Confirmed). Its two stated objectives are: (i) prepare and maintain a Career Development Plan and deliver structured transferable-skills training across MSCA-PF mandatory dimensions; and (ii) facilitate two-way transfer of knowledge between fellow and host through methods seminars and co-supervision of at minimum one MSc thesis (WP4 objectives, wp_structure.json, Confirmed by task structure; the MSc co-supervision target is an OBJ-5 scaffold value, objectives.json, evidence_strength: unconfirmed, spine-dependent).

The lead partner for WP4 is [SUPERVISOR — Unresolved] (wp_structure.json, WP4 lead_partner: SUPERVISOR, Confirmed by role token). This is not incidental: WP4 being led by the supervisor rather than by the fellow reflects SR-07's explicit requirement that the CDP be established jointly by supervisor(s) and researcher, and that training delivery is a supervisory responsibility that cannot be delegated entirely to the fellow. The host ([HOST — Unresolved]) and the fellow are contributing partners in WP4 (contributing_partners: HOST, FELLOW; wp_structure.json, Confirmed).

WP4 contains three tasks:

- **T4-01 — Prepare and maintain Career Development Plan** (responsible: [SUPERVISOR — Unresolved]; contributing: fellow; wp_structure.json, Confirmed). CDP co-authored jointly at the start of the action and maintained through two formal review cycles. The supervisor's responsible-partner assignment makes D4-01's delivery attributable to the supervisor as a formal work-package commitment, not only to the fellow.

- **T4-02 — Deliver transferable skills training programme** (responsible: [SUPERVISOR — Unresolved]; contributing: [HOST — Unresolved]; wp_structure.json, Confirmed). The training programme, structured against the three mandatory SR-06 dimensions, is delivered under supervisory responsibility with the host's institutional resources. This assignment makes the training programme a supervisory commitment rather than a self-organised programme.

- **T4-03 — Facilitate two-way knowledge transfer activities** (responsible: fellow; contributing: [SUPERVISOR — Unresolved]; wp_structure.json, Confirmed). The fellow leads the transfer activities directed toward the host group — methods seminars, joint presentations — under supervisory facilitation.

The single formal deliverable from WP4 is D4-01 — the Career Development Plan — due at month 3 (wp_structure.json, Confirmed; consistent with SR-07's requirement for delivery at the beginning of the action). Month-3 delivery is substantively important: it defines the training trajectory before the research ramp-up reaches its most demanding phase (diagnostic model calibration target MS2, month 12, milestones_seed.json, Confirmed). A CDP delivered at month 3 governs the training programme prospectively; a CDP delivered at month 12 describes what training happened to occur.

---

### The Career Development Plan: structure, content, and review cycle

The CDP is co-authored jointly by [SUPERVISOR — Unresolved] and the fellow (SR-07, Confirmed, scope_requirements.json; T4-01, wp_structure.json, Confirmed). Joint authorship is an SR-07 requirement, not a formality: it requires an actual dialogue about the researcher's career needs and the supervisor's training capacity, producing a document that is neither a generic template nor a researcher's self-assessment submitted for passive counter-signature. The CDP must address six content dimensions per SR-07: research objectives; training and career needs; transferable skills; teaching activities; publications planning; and participation in open science events.

**Research objectives** in the CDP are the four research objectives (OBJ-1 through OBJ-4; objectives.json, Confirmed for OBJ-1, OBJ-2, OBJ-3 source_grounded; Inferred for OBJ-4) and the milestone schedule (MS1–MS6; milestones_seed.json; MS1, MS2, MS3, MS5 Confirmed source_grounded; MS4, MS6 Inferred synthesis), providing a shared reference document for monitoring progress at the M12 and M24 checkpoints.

**Training and career needs** are jointly assessed at CDP co-authorship. For this fellowship the fellow's entry profile (probabilistic ML expertise; prior uncertainty-aware AquaCrop calibration, PI Role, METH-PART-003, Inferred; doi:10.1016/j.envsoft.2022.105556) and the host's attributed competences (geoinformatics, environmental-physics modelling, field-scale spatial data infrastructure; Inferred from concept_note.md, strategic_positioning.md; spine-dependent) together determine which needs are already partially met and which must be actively developed. Confirmed identities are required to complete this assessment.

**Transferable skills** must address the three mandatory SR-06 dimensions. **Teaching activities** are addressed through the planned MSc thesis co-supervision at [HOST — Unresolved] [OBJ-5 scaffold, synthetic/spine-dependent] and through the methods seminars (T4-03). **Publications planning** covers the publication timeline, authorship allocation and target journals. **Open science events** are addressed through conference presentations [OBJ-5 scaffold, synthetic/spine-dependent] and the open-access publication commitment at MS6 (Inferred, milestones_seed.json).

The CDP is reviewed and updated at month 12 and month 24 [DURATION — Unresolved; operator-declared 24 months, SYN-SPINE-01]. The month-12 review aligns with MS2 (milestones_seed.json, Confirmed, source_grounded): the first major research milestone is a natural recalibration point at which emerging training gaps can be incorporated into months 12–24. The month-24 review aligns with MS6 (Inferred, milestones_seed.json) and serves as the terminal career development assessment.

A practical observation evaluators should note: the month-3 CDP delivery is a proxy indicator of supervisory arrangement quality. A supervisor who is on extended leave, managing excessive group sizes, or lacking a formed view of the fellowship's training requirements cannot jointly produce a credible CDP by month 3. This timeline is a substantive test of the supervisory arrangement's practical depth — a test assessable only against confirmed supervisor identity and availability, neither of which is available from current Tier 3 data.

---

### Supervisor qualifications, track record and experience supervising at advanced level

**Evaluator-critical unresolved gap.** The supervisor's identity, publication record, research profile, and documented experience supervising researchers at postdoctoral level are absent from all source vault nodes (confirmation_checklist.json, SUPERVISOR: source_vault_nodes: []; what_source_says: 'No supervisor appears ANYWHERE in the vault'). The synthetic placeholder [SUPERVISOR — Unresolved; Prof. Dr. Gábor Nagy [SYNTHETIC], ELTE, environmental physics/geoinformatics] occupies the WP4 lead and contributing-partner positions in WP1, WP2, and WP3 without supplying any confirmed competence, publication, or supervision-history content.

This is the single most consequential gap in this sub-section. MSCA-PF evaluators assess whether the confirmed supervisor (i) has an established research profile in at least a relevant subdomain of the project's disciplines, and (ii) has a documented track record of successfully supervising researchers at postdoctoral level to career outcomes within academia and beyond. An evaluator who cannot verify both criteria for a named supervisor will correctly score this sub-criterion below its potential regardless of the structural quality of the training architecture.

The structural design of the fellowship provides three partial mitigations, none of which removes the requirement for confirmed supervisor evidence:

**Mitigation 1 — Fellow as primary methodological contributor.** The fellow leads all four research work packages (WP1, WP2, WP3, WP5; wp_structure.json, Confirmed) and brings the primary methodological contribution. The supervisor's research role is as a contributing partner in WP1 (T1-02, T1-03), WP2 (T2-01), and WP3 (T3-01, T3-02) and lead of WP4. This allocation means the fellowship does not require the supervisor to be at the probabilistic ML or Bayesian crop-modelling frontier; it requires research oversight, intellectual challenge, methodological feedback, and training governance.

**Mitigation 2 — Host's geoinformatics infrastructure as complement.** [HOST — Unresolved]'s attributed geoinformatics and environmental-modelling competences (Inferred from concept_note.md, strategic_positioning.md; spine-dependent; must be confirmed) are most directly relevant to WP3 field validation (T3-01 contributing: HOST and SUPERVISOR; wp_structure.json, Confirmed), creating a legitimate partial specialisation within the supervisory arrangement if the confirmed supervisor's expertise is stronger in the geospatial domain than in probabilistic ML.

**Mitigation 3 — CDP as network-augmentation governance instrument.** The CDP (SR-07, Confirmed) provides the governance mechanism through which gaps between the supervisor's immediate expertise and the fellowship's full disciplinary scope can be addressed through collaborations, visiting lecturers, external training courses, or conference-based interactions. The supervisor need not be individually expert across all four disciplines if the CDP specifies how each training need is met and by whom.

None of these mitigations substitutes for confirmed supervisor identity and track record. The confirmed supervisor's publication record in at least one of {Earth observation/geoinformatics, probabilistic ML, crop modelling/agricultural hydrology}, documented prior postdoctoral supervision with verifiable supervisee career outcomes, and confirmed availability within [HOST — Unresolved]'s research environment must be provided before this sub-section can be finalised.

---

### Scientific training embedded in the research programme

The most substantive training component is not a formal course syllabus but the research programme itself. Designing, calibrating, and validating the four-stage observation-to-decision pipeline (OBJ-1 through OBJ-4; objectives.json) requires active research-grade proficiency across four disciplines. The research tasks in WP1, WP2, and WP3 are the primary vehicle through which those proficiencies are consolidated and extended.

**WP1 — Earth observation and probabilistic machine learning (T1-01, T1-02, T1-03; wp_structure.json, Confirmed).** T1-01 (Acquire and harmonise EO and ground sensor data) develops research-grade satellite data engineering: temporal compositing across Sentinel-1 (approximately 6-day repeat) and Sentinel-2 (approximately 5-day repeat) overpass cycles, atmospheric correction, cloud masking for optical gaps compensated by SAR (RISK-03, Inferred, risks.json), geometric co-registration, and heterogeneous sensor data harmonisation. T1-02 (Implement probabilistic fusion model, Route A/B) is the core probabilistic ML training vehicle. Implementing the candidate model families — Bayesian hierarchical models and Gaussian processes (concept_note.md, source_grounded) — to produce full posterior distributions over the latent field state requires prior specification for geophysical quantities, likelihood design for heterogeneous multi-sensor inputs, posterior inference algorithm selection, diagnostic assessment of convergence and calibration, and handling asynchronous multi-resolution covariate streams. T1-03 (Calibrate and evaluate diagnostic branch output) develops evaluation methodology: designing calibration metrics (RQ5, Confirmed as open, confirmation_checklist.json), documenting the protocol for reproducibility, and producing deliverable D1-01 (due month 14; wp_structure.json, Confirmed). Each task develops a distinct, transferable research competence extending the fellow's capabilities beyond what the prior calibration method (doi:10.1016/j.envsoft.2022.105556; PI Role, METH-PART-003, Inferred) required.

**WP2 — Crop physiology, agricultural economics, and software integration (T2-01, T2-02, T2-03; wp_structure.json, Confirmed).** T2-01 (Implement uncertainty-aware AquaCrop calibration) extends the prior calibration expertise to a structurally more complex setting: the input is now an uncertain posterior from WP1 rather than a deterministic observation, and calibration must propagate that input uncertainty into the AquaCrop parameter posterior (METH-DEC-002, source_grounded, concept_note.md). This requires understanding AquaCrop soil-crop parameterisations at the level of knowing which parameters are most calibration-sensitive and how to specify informative priors from agronomic knowledge. T2-02 (Build counterfactual irrigation simulation and decision engine) introduces agricultural economics training: the counterfactual simulation runs over a weather ensemble and the recommendation scores candidate decisions by expected profit — expected crop value minus full irrigation cost (METH-DEC-005, METH-DEC-006, source_grounded, concept_note.md). This requires operationalising an economic decision criterion that operates correctly on the full distribution of AquaCrop outputs across the weather ensemble. T2-03 (Integrate diagnosis and decision into research demonstrator) trains software architecture and research-communication design: modular pipeline decomposition, demonstrator user interface design, and making probabilistic uncertainty interpretable to non-statistician farming practitioners.

**WP3 — Field validation design and uncertainty calibration assessment (T3-01, T3-02; wp_structure.json, Confirmed).** T3-01 (Design validation protocol and ground truth collection; contributing: HOST and SUPERVISOR) trains field-experiment design for probabilistic model validation: specifying necessary and sufficient ground-truth measurements (RQ4, Confirmed as open), designing the sampling protocol, co-ordinating with host and supervisor as contributing partners. T3-02 (Assess uncertainty calibration against field data) trains probabilistic model evaluation methodology: computing empirical prediction-interval coverage at stated nominal levels (RQ5, Confirmed as open), applying proper scoring rules, executing the pre-registered Route B patch-covariation test (RQ9, Confirmed as open; Control Stand Variant, METH-ROUTE-003, source_grounded, concept_note.md), and applying pilot-success criteria (RQ7, Confirmed as open). These probabilistic model evaluation competences are transferable across environmental modelling disciplines well beyond crop water stress.

A fellow who completes OBJ-1 through OBJ-3 will have acquired working research competences across five specific sub-areas — EO data engineering, probabilistic ML for environmental inference, AquaCrop uncertainty analysis, agricultural economics decision criterion design, and probabilistic calibration diagnostics — representing a substantial expansion of the research profile relative to the entry point.

---

### The three mandatory SR-06 transferable-skills dimensions

SR-06 (scope_requirements.json, Confirmed, mandatory) requires three classes of key transferable skills. All three are addressed as integral dimensions of the research work plan.

**Dimension 1 — Digital skills, including responsible use of generative AI (SR-06, CC-10, CC-11; scope_requirements.json, Confirmed).**

At the research-computing level, T1-02 and T1-03 in WP1 provide the primary digital skills formation through the full scientific Python stack for probabilistic ML, GPU-accelerated posterior sampling, the GDAL/Rasterio ecosystem for EO data access, automated unit testing of probabilistic model components, and version-controlled collaborative software development.

Responsible generative AI use is explicitly named in SR-06 ('digital skills (e.g. generative AI)'; Confirmed). This training dimension is operationalised through the fellow's active engagement during T1-02, T2-01, and the open research software development tasks with the specific challenges of using LLM code assistants in scientific research contexts. The responsible-use discipline for this project is not merely an ethics posture but a methodological necessity: unattributed AI-generated code whose correctness has not been independently verified breaks the Uncertainty Chain's (METH-CORE-004, source_grounded) scientific validity claim. Responsible use is operationalised as a concrete research-quality discipline: AI-assisted code components are independently tested against known reference outputs, documented, and attributed in the public repository before incorporation into the research codebase — verifiable by inspection of the repository commit history and test suite.

At the digital collaboration and FAIR data platform level (CC-11, Confirmed), the open research software development practices and the FAIR Data Management Plan (D5-01, T5-01, WP5; due month 6; MS1, milestones_seed.json, Confirmed, source_grounded) develop the systematic FAIR data management competences, including format standards, metadata schema design, versioning conventions, repository access configuration, and long-term accessibility planning.

**Dimension 2 — Knowledge valorisation and innovation/entrepreneurship (SR-06; Confirmed).**

Knowledge valorisation training is embedded in T2-03 (WP2; Confirmed). Building the standalone research demonstrator web MVP — presenting probabilistic irrigation recommendations to a non-statistician farming practitioner audience — requires the fellow to engage with the translational gap between a calibrated research model and a form of knowledge accessible to potential users. The demonstrator is explicitly a research artefact (OBJ-4; objectives.json, Inferred, synthesis; TRL open at RQ10), not a market-ready product; but the exercise of making the framework's probabilistic outputs interpretable requires user-requirement analysis, interface design for uncertain information, and communication of distributional predictions to domain-expert non-statisticians — the competences knowledge-valorisation training develops.

Engagement with [VALIDATION_PARTNER — Unresolved; synthetic value: AgroVIR Kft. [SYNTHETIC ARRANGEMENT]; must be confirmed] during WP3 field validation provides inter-sectoral learning: farming practitioners frame the irrigation decision in terms of operational constraints, cash-flow scheduling, and agronomic risk tolerances that differ substantially from the academic expected-profit-maximisation framing. The fellow's engagement with those differences through T3-01 and T2-03 is the inter-sectoral dimension feeding EO-02 (Inferred mapping, concept_refinement_summary.json). The validation partner is Unresolved (confirmation_checklist.json, VALIDATION_PARTNER) and the specific inter-sectoral training it enables cannot be fully specified until confirmed.

**Dimension 3 — Research integrity, open-science ethics and FAIR data management (SR-06, CC-10, CC-11; Confirmed).**

Research integrity training is structured into the project methodology through five interlocking obligations:

*DMP design and delivery (T5-01; D5-01, due month 6; MS1, milestones_seed.json, Confirmed, source_grounded).* Writing the FAIR DMP before the sensor pipeline is built (T1-01) requires active early decisions about data format standards, metadata schemas, versioning conventions, access conditions, and long-term repository arrangements for all project data — constraining engineering choices in T1-01 and T1-02 from inception. The month-6 DMP delivery (CC-10, CC-11, scope_requirements.json, Confirmed) mandates that research-integrity thinking governs research-engineering design from the project's start. The DMP satisfies EO-07 (Confirmed mapping, concept_refinement_summary.json) through the structured FAIR-compliant data assets it defines.

*Open research software.* The diagnostic model (WP1, T1-02), uncertainty-aware AquaCrop calibration module (WP2, T2-01), counterfactual simulation engine (WP2, T2-02), and research demonstrator (WP2, T2-03) are developed as open-source software under FAIR-compliant licences. Open-source development requires that every design decision is attributable and inspectable, automated unit tests verify correctness of probabilistic inference components, and documentation enables independent deployment — necessary conditions for the scientific validity of the calibration claim. A closed-source implementation of the Uncertainty Chain (METH-CORE-004, source_grounded) cannot be accepted or rejected by the community because chain integrity cannot be verified without inspecting the implementation.

*Validation protocol design for reproducibility.* The field validation protocol (T3-01, WP3) is designed for third-party reproducibility from inception: specifying what ground truth is collected (RQ4, Confirmed as open), how uncertainty is evaluated (RQ5, Confirmed as open), what pilot-success criteria apply (RQ7, Confirmed as open), and how Route B covariation is tested (RQ9, Confirmed as open; Control Stand Variant, METH-ROUTE-003, source_grounded). Publishing the protocol, data, model implementation, and validation results together enables independent replication of the calibration finding — the highest available standard of research integrity for an empirical modelling study.

*Publication ethics.* The CDP (SR-07, Confirmed) explicitly covers publications planning as one of its six content dimensions, making authorship attribution, peer-review obligations, data availability statements, and open-access requirements a structured component of the supervisory plan.

*Societal engagement.* The research demonstrator (OBJ-4, Inferred, synthesis) and engagement with practitioner users during T2-03 constitute the primary societal engagement training. International conference presentations [OBJ-5 scaffold, synthetic/spine-dependent] and the open-access publication at MS6 (Inferred, milestones_seed.json) satisfy academic networking and communication dimensions, contributing to EO-03 (Inferred mapping, concept_refinement_summary.json).

---

### Two-way transfer of knowledge between researcher and host

**Applicable transfer model and fellowship-type dependency.** The transfer model is determined by the fellowship type: a European Fellowship requires two-way transfer between researcher and host (SR-02, Confirmed, scope_requirements.json); a Global Fellowship would require three-way transfer between researcher, outgoing host, and return-phase associated partner (SR-03, Confirmed). FELLOWSHIP_TYPE is Unresolved (confirmation_checklist.json; still_requires_real_confirmation: true). The synthetic working spine derives a European Fellowship from the intra-EU mobility (BG → HU), which is an EF by definition — but this derivation rests on a synthetic host. If the real host is in a non-associated Third Country, the fellowship type becomes a Global Fellowship and the transfer analysis changes structurally. The two-way transfer content below is drafted on the EF (synthetic) assumption and must be revised once the confirmed host determines the fellowship type.

On the EF assumption, EO-07 (Stronger R&I capacity; better transfer of knowledge; Confirmed, expected_outcomes.json) is satisfied by the two-way transfer design. EO-07 is the only expected outcome in the programme's Tier 2B expected_outcomes.json for which concept_refinement_summary.json records a Confirmed (not Inferred) mapping, because the concept uses the phrase 'transfer of knowledge' verbatim in the supervision section title (concept_refinement_summary.json, EO-07 mapping: 'The concept explicitly uses the phrase "transfer of knowledge" verbatim in the section title'). The two-way transfer design is therefore the evaluator's strongest vocabulary-aligned evidence link between this proposal and the call's expected outcomes.

**Fellow to host — transfer content, mechanism and evidence.**

The fellow transfers two specific, vault-grounded technical contributions to [HOST — Unresolved]'s research group:

*Transfer contribution 1 — Uncertainty-aware AquaCrop calibration method.* The fellow brings the peer-reviewed uncertainty-aware AquaCrop calibration methodology (doi:10.1016/j.envsoft.2022.105556; referenced in concept_note.md as 'the fellow-attributed method'; PI Role, METH-PART-003, Inferred from first-person authorship of the design narrative). This prior method establishes that AquaCrop can be calibrated while retaining an explicit parameter posterior — the technical prerequisite for OBJ-2 and for Uncertainty Chain integrity at the AquaCrop model interface (METH-CORE-004, source_grounded, concept_note.md). The fellowship's extension — accepting an uncertain posterior field-state input from WP1 rather than a deterministic input — is a more complex application that demonstrates the method's generality and transfers that extended capability into the host group. The transfer occurs through the research work visible to the host group via their WP1 (T1-02, T1-03) and WP2 (T2-01) contributing-partner roles, not merely through a publication citation.

*Transfer contribution 2 — Probabilistic machine learning competences for multi-sensor crop-water modelling.* The fellow brings probabilistic ML expertise applied to multi-source EO fusion for crop-water-state estimation — not described as existing within [HOST — Unresolved]'s group (concept_note.md, strategic_positioning.md; Inferred from synthetic spine). Transfer occurs through: (i) the research work itself, making design rationale and implementation choices visible to host group members through their contributing-partner roles; and (ii) at minimum two methods seminars delivered by the fellow at [HOST — Unresolved]'s group on uncertainty-aware crop-water modelling and probabilistic fusion [OBJ-5 measurable target, objectives.json, synthetic/spine-dependent; structural intent confirmed from concept_note.md and strategic_positioning.md section 1.3].

Evidence base for fellow-to-host transfer: (a) the demonstrable prior publication (doi:10.1016/j.envsoft.2022.105556; PI Role, METH-PART-003, Inferred) as the source of the transferred expertise; (b) host group contributing-partner roles in WP1–WP3 (wp_structure.json, Confirmed) providing direct visibility of the methodology as applied; (c) the methods seminars as structured, verifiable knowledge-transfer events (T4-03, WP4, Confirmed; target count spine-dependent, to be confirmed in D4-01).

**Host to fellow — transfer content, mechanism and evidence.**

[HOST — Unresolved]'s group transfers to the fellow competences in geoinformatics, field-scale geospatial data collection, and spatial data infrastructure (Inferred from concept_note.md, strategic_positioning.md; attributed competences of the synthetic host; must be confirmed with real host identity). These competences are essential for WP3 field validation (OBJ-3, Confirmed, source_grounded) and are disciplines the fellow does not bring from the prior calibration method.

The host-to-fellow transfer is structurally embedded in the fellow's co-leadership of WP3 validation tasks:

- **T3-01 (Design validation protocol; responsible: fellow; contributing: HOST and SUPERVISOR; wp_structure.json, Confirmed):** The host's contributing role means the host group's field-data collection competences, geospatial survey infrastructure, and local agricultural-environment knowledge are actively integrated into the protocol design. The fellow cannot design a credible ground-truth collection protocol for the target field sites without the host group's knowledge of those sites — making T3-01 the primary mechanism through which host geospatial and field-data competences are transferred to the fellow through a collaborative applied-research task.

- **T3-02 (Assess uncertainty calibration against field data; responsible: fellow; contributing: SUPERVISOR; wp_structure.json, Confirmed):** The calibration assessment uses data whose collection the host facilitated through T3-01, and the host's data-infrastructure contribution flows through into the quality of the calibration evidence.

The host-to-fellow transfer also includes an academic mentorship dimension through co-supervision of at minimum one MSc thesis at [HOST — Unresolved] [OBJ-5 measurable target, objectives.json, synthetic/spine-dependent; strategic_positioning.md section 2.1]. Co-supervising an MSc thesis within the host's programme embeds the fellow in the host's academic supervision governance, student mentoring norms, and graduate education standards — a distinct career development dimension acquired only through situated participation in the host's teaching activities. This is the primary EO-08 mechanism (Regular feedback of research results into teaching; Confirmed, expected_outcomes.json; Inferred mapping, concept_refinement_summary.json): the MSc thesis topic, grounded in the fellowship's uncertainty-aware crop-water modelling findings, feeds those research results directly into the host's student training programme.

**Five verifiable evidence components for the two-way transfer:**

1. **D4-01 (CDP, due month 3; wp_structure.json, Confirmed; SR-07, Confirmed):** CDP specifies knowledge-transfer obligations of both supervisor and fellow from month 3, making the planned transfer explicitly accountable from the action's start.

2. **T4-03 (wp_structure.json, Confirmed):** A dedicated work-plan task with the fellow as responsible partner and supervisor as contributing partner, creating a tracked task scope for the transfer activities.

3. **Methods seminars at [HOST — Unresolved]** [OBJ-5 measurable target, objectives.json, synthetic/spine-dependent; EO-07 Confirmed mapping, concept_refinement_summary.json]: At minimum two methods seminars on uncertainty-aware crop-water modelling and probabilistic fusion delivered by the fellow to the host's research group. Verifiable by seminar records.

4. **Co-authored publications between fellow and [SUPERVISOR — Unresolved]** [Inferred from OBJ-5 publication targets, objectives.json, synthetic/spine-dependent; EO-07 mapping, concept_refinement_summary.json]: joint publications are the most durable evidence of genuine two-way intellectual exchange. Verifiable by authorship records.

5. **Co-supervision of ≥1 MSc thesis at [HOST — Unresolved]** [OBJ-5 measurable target, objectives.json, synthetic/spine-dependent]: verifiable by thesis registration records at the host institution.

All five are verifiable activities. Components 3–5 carry spine-dependent targets requiring confirmed SUPERVISOR, HOST, and FELLOW identities before they can be finalised.

The two-way transfer design satisfies EO-07 (Confirmed mapping, concept_refinement_summary.json), contributes to EO-05 (Enhanced quality and sustainability of research training; Inferred mapping, concept_refinement_summary.json) through the structured CDP and supervisor-led WP4 governance, and contributes to EO-08 (Inferred mapping, concept_refinement_summary.json) through the MSc thesis co-supervision and methods-seminar channels. EO-04 (Charter alignment; Confirmed, expected_outcomes.json; Assumed mapping, concept_refinement_summary.json) requires an explicit Charter compliance statement from [HOST — Unresolved] that is absent from all current Tier 3 documents (concept_refinement_summary.json EO-04: 'Neither "European Charter for Researchers" nor "working conditions" appears anywhere in the concept corpus') and must be provided once the host is confirmed.

---

### Secondment and non-academic placement: not proposed

No secondment is proposed. The fellowship is fully structured as research and training at [HOST — Unresolved] across the 24-month working scaffold [DURATION — Unresolved; operator-declared 24 months, SYN-SPINE-01], with no secondment period. SR-04 (scope_requirements.json, Confirmed, non-mandatory) permits secondments for European Fellowships not exceeding half the requested duration; this provision is not invoked (CC-04 not_applicable, concept_refinement_summary.json). The rationale is that the 24-month timeline is fully occupied by four research objectives and the structured training programme; adding a secondment would introduce coordination costs and a geographic interruption to the supervisory relationship without providing research access not available at [HOST — Unresolved]. The freely available ESA Copernicus data infrastructure (Sentinel-1, Sentinel-2; METH-INFRA-002, source_grounded, concept_note.md) and [HOST — Unresolved]'s attributed geospatial infrastructure provide the primary research access requirements.

No non-academic sector placement is proposed. SR-05 (scope_requirements.json, Confirmed, non-mandatory) permits an optional period of up to six months for a non-academic sector placement at the end of the project; this provision is not invoked (CC-07 not_applicable, concept_refinement_summary.json). The validation partner [VALIDATION_PARTNER — Unresolved; synthetic value: AgroVIR Kft. **EO-01 / EI-01** (Increased research and transferable skills → improved employability; Confirmed, expected_outcomes.json, expected_impacts.json; Confirmed mapping, concept_refinement_summary.json): The CDP (D4-01, month 3; SR-07, Confirmed), the three-dimension SR-06 training programme (Confirmed), and the scientific training embedded in WP1–WP3 provide a comprehensive documented training record.

### Summary assessment for evaluators

The structural training architecture of this fellowship is evaluator-coherent and programme-compliant: WP4 is a fully specified work package with three tasks, a month-3 deliverable (CDP), a supervisor-led governance model, and a two-way transfer design with five verifiable evidence components. All three mandatory SR-06 transferable-skills dimensions are addressed through specific research tasks embedded in the work plan, making training integral to the research programme. The CDP structure satisfies SR-07's full content specification. EO-07 is satisfied with a Confirmed vocabulary mapping — the strongest alignment in the expected outcomes register. The non-invocation of the optional secondment and non-academic placement provisions is a reasoned design choice, not an oversight.

The single evaluator-critical gap — not addressable by structural design — is the supervisor's identity, qualifications, and track record. The confirmed supervisor's publication record in a relevant domain, documented prior success in postdoctoral supervision, and confirmed availability within the host institution's research environment are the evidence base evaluators require for this sub-criterion. That evidence base is currently absent from all Tier 3 source data (SUPERVISOR: source_vault_nodes: []; confirmation_checklist.json). Until a real supervisor is confirmed and their track record incorporated into the Tier 3 project instantiation, the score for this sub-section is limited by the structural design's quality — which is strong — rather than by the supervisor's verified credentials — which remain entirely unknown.
